A1.justification: Both readable, 11-page PDFs describe the same GASLIGHT work. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement. V3 refers the BtP-HDR qualitative examples shown in v1 Figure 6 to unavailable supplementary material, limiting comparison of that portion; the remaining material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 report original relighting evaluations on Si-HDR, BtP-HDR and two PanoHDR-NeRF scenes, with numerical results and generated images.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark results and adds a GlowGAN comparison, an estimator-replacement ablation, a consistency experiment and text-to-HDR demonstrations.

M1.justification: Although the two-stage backbone remains, v1's log-space L2 reconstruction objective becomes L1 plus SSIM on LDR pixels in v3. Object insertion changes from treating all Gaussians as emitters to making only those above intensity 1 emitters, with the remainder diffuse. Section 5.2 also introduces a LucidDreamer-based text-input extension.

E1.justification: The training data and principal evaluation datasets remain unchanged. V3 adds qualitative text-to-HDR environment generation using LucidDreamer and an artificially clamped-input consistency scenario. The new landscape comparison uses a subset of existing Si-HDR coverage.

E2.justification: V3 newly evaluates GlowGAN on selected Si-HDR landscapes in Table 4 and an Ours+LaNet variant alongside PanoHDR-NeRF and the full method in Table 6. The original Table 3 comparator set and the principal PanoHDR-NeRF comparison remain.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands beyond rendered-image MSE/PSNR to angular error, direct-image HDR-VDP-3 and PU21-PIQE, and PU21-PSNR for 3D reconstruction. New protocols include a 23-image landscape subset with specialized GlowGAN checkpoints, manually clamped HDR inputs and estimator substitution. The original Si-HDR filtering and main training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 discusses consistency without testing it directly. New Section 4.4 tests reconstruction after manually clamping HDR predictions to 1 (Figure 6) and replaces the proposed HDR estimator with LaNet (Table 6). These add substantive robustness and component-attribution evidence absent from v1.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V3 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 retains its original MSE/PSNR values but adds angular and perceptual results. The 3D comparison changes numerically: Chess room MSE becomes 0.0026 from 0.0053 for GASLIGHT and 0.0134 from 0.0247 for PanoHDR-NeRF. These revisions are insufficiently explained for attributing a same-setting gain. GlowGAN, ablation and application results are also added.

T1.justification: V1 Equation 1 explicitly defines a log-transformed L2 objective; v3 removes that definition and specifies a different L1/SSIM objective in prose. Exposure-scaling and HDR-fusion mathematics remain unchanged, and neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of diffusion-based HDR estimation, spatially varying Gaussian-Splat lighting, strong HDR/relighting performance and a calibrated unsaturated dataset. The additional experiments and application do not materially redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: V3 replaces the explanation of weaker BtP-HDR PSNR based on lower indoor dynamic range with one based on fixed white balance and color distribution shift. It strengthens the spherical-harmonic consistency interpretation and newly states that accurate near-field ray-traced lighting is impractical for real-time use.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising code after acceptance to stating availability through a project link. V3 newly reports roughly five recursive exposure iterations and expresses inference timing as approximately 4 seconds per relative EV, versus approximately 40 seconds total in v1; this does not establish a speedup.

R1.justification: V3 removes the camera-pose literature paragraph and its citations, while adding spherical-Gaussian and explicit-lighting discussion, including SF3D, PhySG and GS-ID, plus inverse-rendering and metric references. This locally refocuses related work while retaining the main positioning against HDR-GS and PanoHDR-NeRF.

P1.justification: V3 tightens grammar and condenses several explanatory paragraphs while preserving the main narrative and section order. It removes the camera-pose paragraph, turns Section 3.2 into an unnumbered heading, adds Section 4.4 and divides applications into Sections 5.1–5.2.

P2.justification: V3 expands Table 3, transposes and expands the former Table 4 as Table 5, and adds Tables 4 and 6. It replaces Figure 1, vertically stacks Figure 2 and adds Figures 6–8. V1's BtP-HDR Figure 6 is absent from the supplied v3 and referred to an unavailable supplement.

improvement.justification: The added direct-HDR metrics and LaNet substitution control strengthen v1's limited evidence about HDR quality and the contributions of estimation versus representation. Code-access information and practical limitations also improve documentation. These gains are tempered by unexplained 3D-score revisions, less explicit specification of the new loss, and a retained all-emitters limitation that conflicts with the thresholded rendering procedure in Section 5.1.
